leuk.stan beside the data (the help page holds only the folder README): Cox regression as a counting process, poisson_lpmf(dN[i, j] | Y[i, j] * exp(beta * Z[i]) * dL0[j]) with Y and dN built from obs_t and fail; the survival time obs_t is the outcome and fail its failure indicator.

mice.stan beside the data (the help page holds only the folder README): Weibull regression t_uncensored[n] ~ weibull(r, exp(-beta[group_uncensored[n]] / r)), the censored mice being arrays outside the table.
pump.stan beside the data (the help page holds only the folder README): x ~ poisson(theta .* t) with theta ~ gamma(alpha, beta), t each pump's exposure.
stacks_a_normal.stan beside the data (the help page holds only the folder README): Y ~ normal(mu, sigma) with mu = beta0 + z * beta, z the standardized x_1 to x_3.

air.stan beside the data (the help page holds only the folder README): y ~ binomial_logit(n, theta1 + theta2 * X) with the latent exposure X ~ normal(alpha + beta * Z, sigma); y counts the successes and n stays the trials.

beetles_cloglog.stan beside the data (the help page holds only the folder README): r ~ binomial(n, p) with p[i] = inv_cloglog(alpha_star + beta * centered_x[i]); r counts the successes and n stays the trials.

RULE GAP: cervix.stan.0 and cervix2.stan beside the data model the three binary columns together, xc ~ bernoulli(q), dc ~ bernoulli_logit(beta0C + beta * xc) and wc ~ bernoulli(phi[xc + 1, dc + 1]), a case-control logistic regression with a misclassified exposure; named dc, the disease status that regression explains, though the joint-analysis case could read none.

hearts.stan beside the data (the help page holds only the folder README): a zero-inflated binomial, log(theta + (1 - theta) * pow(1 - p, t[i])) for y[i] == 0, else log1m_theta + binomial_lpmf(y[i] | t[i], p); y counts the successes and t stays the trials.

none, the outcome is no column of the table: mvn_orange.stan beside the data fits Y[k, n] ~ normal(phi[k, 1] / (1 + phi[k, 2] * exp(phi[k, 3] * x[n])), sigma_C), but Y and x are arrays outside the table, which holds only the prior's hyperparameters (mu_var_prior, invR, mu_m_prior).

pines.stan beside the data (the help page holds only the folder README): a choice between normal_lpdf(y_std | alpha + beta * x_std, sigma[1]) and normal_lpdf(y_std | gamma + delta * z_std, sigma[2]), y_std the standardized y.

stagnant.stan beside the data (the help page holds only the folder README): change-point regression normal_lpdf(Y | mu, sigma) with mu[n] = alpha + beta[1 or 2] * (x[n] - x[k]), mixed over the change point k.
